content:
The test image shows a mango leaf with distinct, dark, irregular spots. Consulting the part index reveals that all four potential diseases—Anthracnose, Die_Back, Powdery_Mildew, and Sooty_Mould—can affect leaves.

A review of the symptom descriptions points strongly toward Anthracnose, which is characterized by "small, black, and irregular" spots on leaves that expand into dead areas. This aligns well with the visual evidence. In contrast, Die_Back involves leaf rolling and a scorched look, Sooty_Mould is a superficial dark coating, and Powdery_Mildew would appear as a white powder; none of these match the test image.

To confirm, I examined a reference image for Anthracnose (`Prepared_Dataset/Mango_Leaf/Anthracnose/leaf/Mango_Leaf_14.jpg`). While it depicted a more advanced stage of the disease with necrotic areas falling out, the underlying lesion type is consistent with the initial spots seen in the test image. The evidence strongly supports a classification of Anthracnose.
